           U3 LANDOWNERS’ RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS’ OBJECTIONS
               TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF CHRIS ROWNTREE

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

       3 Trees Ranch Family LP and U3 Landowners (U3 Landowners) hereby file this Response
to Applicants’ objections to the Direct Testimony of Chris Rowntree, and respectfully show as
follows:

                          I.   INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY

       Applicants seek to exclude testimony and exhibits concerning conditions existing on and
along Link U3, including the fact that Link U3 would cross an existing quarry on Tract 4928 and
remove recoverable sandstone from productive use within the proposed transmission corridor. The
objections sweep too broadly and should be overruled and the motion to strike denied.
       Mr. Rowntree is a directly affected U3 Landowner and manager of the entity that owns
affected ranch property along Link U3. He may testify from personal knowledge concerning the
property, its existing uses, the location and operation of the quarry, and the practical effects of
placing a new 200-foot transmission corridor across the quarry footprint. Mr. Rowntree also has
engineering training and professional experience evaluating in-place mineral reserves using
volumetric calculations and recovery assumptions. That background qualifies him to explain the
 reserve-volume methodology used in his testimony, which is not offered to determine just
compensation or condemnation damages—it identifies and quantifies a concrete, site-specific
routing impact unique to Link U3: the permanent sterilization of commercially recoverable
sandstone reserves in an existing quarry directly crossed by the proposed right-of-way. That
impact is relevant to the Commission’s route-selection inquiry, including reasonable moderation
of the impact on affected landowners and the community. Applicants’ objections should be
overruled. Alternatively, if the Administrative Law Judges (ALJs) determine Mr. Rowntree’s
ultimate dollar-value ranges are being offered as evidence of compensable loss, any exclusion
should be narrowly confined to that ultimate dollar range.
        Applicants’ objections to “certain attachments” 1 fail for an independent reason: they do not
identify with particularity the specific attachments, passages, or propositions they seek to exclude.
Their objections also improperly target U3 Landowner statements of position, which are argument
rather than evidence, and unspecified filings of neighboring landowners who have now joined U3
Landowners and designated 3 Trees Ranch Family LP as their authorized representative.

II. PRELIMINARY OBJECTION: APPLICANTS’ OBJECTIONS WERE NOT TIMELY
                SERVED AS REQUIRED BY SOAH ORDER NO. 1

        Applicants’ objections to intervenor testimony present a threshold procedural problem
affecting not only U3 Landowners, but potentially every intervenor whose testimony or exhibits
Applicants seek to strike. SOAH Order No. 1 expressly provides that, although ordinary filings
may be served through the PUC Interchange, “motions, responses to motions, and other filings
that request or require action by another party” must be emailed to the party that is the target of
the filing. Applicants’ objections plainly fall within that requirement. They request affirmative
relief against the targeted intervenors—the exclusion of their filed testimony and exhibits—and
require those intervenors to take action to protect their evidentiary presentations.
        SOAH Order No. 6 established May 18, 2026 as the deadline for Applicants to object to
intervenor direct testimony. Applicants filed their objections on the Interchange by that date, but
their certificate of service stated only that the objections were served “via the PUC Interchange.”
Applicants did not email their objections to U3 Landowners’ counsel until after 4:00 p.m. on


1
  See Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation’s Objections to, and
Motion to Strike, Intervenor Testimony at Exhibit A, PDF Page 31 of 39 (May 18, 2026) (“Certain attachments,
including . . . .”) [AIS Item No. 4726].

U3 LANDOWNERS’ RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS’ OBJECTIONS
                                                                                                               2
TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF CHRIS ROWNTREE
 Friday, May 22, 2026—four days after the objection deadline. Thus, as to U3 Landowners and
252 other recipients of Applicants’ late email, Applicants did not complete the service expressly
required by SOAH Order No. 1 until four days after objections were due.
       This was not an inadvertent misunderstanding of the service requirement. In Applicants’
May 19, 2026 Request for Extension of Objections Deadline, Applicants used a materially
different certificate of service, certifying that the motion had been filed on the Interchange “and
served on all parties from whom an action is required via email.” Applicants therefore recognized
that a filing requiring action from another party must be emailed to that party, yet failed to provide
that same required service when seeking to strike intervenors’ testimony and exhibits.
       The defect is broader than the prejudice to U3 Landowners alone. Applicants’ objections
seek relief against numerous intervenors and, on their face, request exclusion of testimony and
exhibits offered by targeted landowners throughout this proceeding. To the extent Applicants
similarly failed to email those objections to other targeted intervenors by the May 18 deadline, the
objections were not timely served as to those parties either. Applicants should not be permitted to
obtain exclusionary relief against landowners based on objections that Applicants themselves
failed to serve in the manner and by the deadline ordered by the ALJs.
       Accordingly, the ALJs should strike or deny Applicants’ objections to intervenor testimony
to the extent Applicants did not timely serve the targeted intervenors by email as required by
SOAH Order No. 1. At minimum, the ALJs should require Applicants to identify every targeted
intervenor who did not receive the required email service by May 18, 2026, and grant each such
party four additional days—equal to the delay experienced by U3 Landowners—from the date of
actual email service to file or supplement any response to Applicants’ objections.
       U3 Landowners respond on the merits solely to protect Mr. Rowntree’s testimony and
exhibits in advance of the hearing and do not waive this procedural objection. Applicants should
not benefit from their noncompliance by obtaining exclusion of Mr. Rowntree’s evidence,
opposing any supplemental evidentiary foundation necessitated by their late notice, or limiting the
ability of any other late-noticed intervenor to respond fully to objections that were not timely
served in compliance with the governing order.




U3 LANDOWNERS’ RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS’ OBJECTIONS
                                                                                                    3
TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF CHRIS ROWNTREE
                                   III. APPLICABLE STANDARD

         In accordance with 16 TAC § 22.221(a), the Texas Rules of Evidence (TRE) applicable in
nonjury civil cases govern this proceeding. When necessary to ascertain facts not reasonably
susceptible of proof under the TRE, evidence not admissible under those rules may be admitted in
a PUC proceeding, unless precluded by statute, if the evidence is of a type commonly relied upon
by reasonably prudent persons in the conduct of their affairs. 2 TRE 701 permits a lay witness to
offer an opinion that is rationally based on the witness’s perception and helpful to clearly
understanding the witness’s testimony or determining a fact in issue.
        This is a transmission-line routing proceeding. Under PURA § 37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC
§ 25.101(b)(3)(B), the Commission considers, among other matters, community values, historical
and aesthetic values, environmental integrity, engineering constraints, costs, and the reasonable
moderation of impacts on affected landowners and the community.

IV. MR. ROWNTREE’S QUARRY ANALYSIS CONCERNS ROUTING IMPACT, NOT
                    CONDEMNATION COMPENSATION

A.      Relevance.
        In attacking relevance, Applicants mischaracterize Mr. Rowntree’s testimony as an effort
to establish compensation. It instead identifies a site-specific routing impact: Link U3 would cross
an existing sandstone quarry and permanently remove recoverable material from productive use
within the proposed 200-foot corridor. This issue is directly relevant to the Commission’s
consideration of prudent avoidance and comparison of land-use and affected-landowner impacts,
even if compensation is reserved for a later forum.
        Applicants object to Mr. Rowntree’s testimony at Page 21: Lines 16–21, testifying about
the value of the saleable material contained within the open sandstone quarry that lies directly
below the proposed Link U3 easement along Tract. The challenged estimate is relevant because
it illustrates the magnitude of a unique, site-specific routing impact created by Link U3—an impact
not identified or addressed in the Application and one that Mr. Rowntree had no opportunity to
raise during the public-participation process because Applicants added Link U3 only after the
public meetings had concluded, without any additional opportunity for affected landowners to


2
  16 Texas Admin. Code § 22.221(a). It should be noted that Commission’s rules are explicitly more lenient than
the Texas Rules of Evidence.

U3 LANDOWNERS’ RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS’ OBJECTIONS
                                                                                                                  4
TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF CHRIS ROWNTREE
 provide input. Mr. Rowntree is not asking the Commission to determine condemnation
compensation or award damages. He is explaining that Link U3 would not merely cross
undeveloped acreage; it would bisect an existing quarry and permanently sterilize valuable and
commercially recoverable stone within the right-of-way footprint. The Commission may consider
that physical and operational land-use impact when comparing routes and evaluating impacts on
affected landowners and the community, thus the testimony is relevant.
B.     Non-Expert Opinion.
       Applicants’ “non-expert-opinion” objection does not support striking the quoted testimony.
Mr. Rowntree’s estimate is based on his personal knowledge of the quarry, his family’s evaluation
of its remaining reserves when acquiring the property, current pricing and operational information
obtained from an experienced local quarry operator selling equivalent stone, and Mr. Rowntree’s
own engineering training and professional experience performing volumetric reserve calculations.
His analysis applies familiar reserve-calculation concepts to the stone rendered unrecoverable by
the proposed right-of-way. The testimony is therefore sufficiently grounded in Mr. Rowntree’s
rational perception, knowledge, and experience, which will assist the ALJs in evaluating the
magnitude of Link U3’s site-specific impact. Mr. Rowntree’s testimony is permissible opinion
testimony by a lay witness.
C.     Hearsay.
       Applicants’ hearsay objection is similarly undeveloped. Applicants identify no specific
out-of-court statement in the quoted testimony and do not identify which pricing, density,
recovery, royalty, or operating-cost input allegedly constitutes inadmissible hearsay.
U3 Landowners do not offer any quarry operator’s statement as stand-alone testimony. Rather,
those inputs form part of the basis for Mr. Rowntree’s disclosed calculation of the magnitude of
stone rendered unrecoverable by the proposed crossing.
D.     Objections Should Be Overruled.
       Applicants’ objections to Page 21: Line 16–21 should be overruled. Alternatively, if the
ALJs determine that the stated dollar range is too closely associated with potential compensation,
any ruling should be limited to that dollar range alone. The testimony that Link U3 would cross
an existing quarry, directly sterilize approximately 7.44 acres of recoverable stone, and impose
additional unquantified operational impacts remains directly relevant to route selection and should
be admitted and considered.


U3 LANDOWNERS’ RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS’ OBJECTIONS
                                                                                                 5
TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF CHRIS ROWNTREE
  V.   RESPONSE TO OBJECTIONS TO PURPORTED “CERTAIN ATTACHMENTS”

A.      Applicants have not identified the challenged attachments or statements with
        sufficient particularity.
        Applicants purport to object to “certain attachments” to Mr. Rowntree’s testimony, but
their description identifies only broad categories: unidentified property-search material,
unspecified information concerning endangered species, an article titled “River Ferry Once
Operated On Hardy Ranch Near Lometa,” unidentified testimony from unnamed neighbors, and
unspecified transcripts from a prior 345-kV proceeding. Applicants do not identify the specific
attachment, exhibit page, testimony page, challenged statement, or proposition for which any
particular material is supposedly offered.
        That is not sufficient to support the extraordinary remedy of striking a landowner’s
evidence. An objection asserting hearsay, relevance, and non-expert opinion must identify the
material being challenged with enough particularity for the responding party to address the
objection and for the ALJs to determine what evidence, if any, is being offered for an inadmissible
purpose. Applicants’ category-level objections leave U3 Landowners and the ALJs to guess what
Applicants want removed from the record and why. The objection should therefore be overruled
as insufficiently specified. At minimum, any ruling should be confined to the specific excerpts
Applicants should not receive relief directed at unspecified attachments or unidentified portions of
other filings.
B.      Applicants cannot obtain an evidentiary ruling striking material contained only in a
        statement of position.
        Applicants object to an article titled “River Ferry Once Operated On Hardy Ranch Near
Lometa,” unspecified “property search data,” “transcripts from a 345kv line hearing,” and
unspecified “chat GPT info on endangered species.” These materials, however, are included in
U3 Landowners’ statements of position, not in Mr. Rowntree’s prefiled evidentiary testimony.
Under 16 TAC § 22.124, a statement of position is the vehicle by which a party opting not to file
testimony states its position in the proceeding. For example, intervenor Les Paul Hardy included
the ferry article in support of his position that a historic structure stands near the proposed route.
Likewise, the referenced property-search and endangered-species materials were included as
support for the affected landowners’ stated positions and concerns regarding Link U3.
        Because the statements of position and their attached background materials have not been
offered as evidence, there is no hearsay, non-expert-opinion, or relevance objection for the ALJs

U3 LANDOWNERS’ RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS’ OBJECTIONS
                                                                                                    6
TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF CHRIS ROWNTREE
 to sustain as an evidentiary matter. Applicants may disagree with the arguments raised in those
statements of position or with the sources upon which the landowners relied in presenting their
concerns. But Applicants cannot obtain an order striking materials as inadmissible evidence when
U3 Landowners have not offered those materials as evidence in the first place.
       The ALJs may assign arguments and materials contained in statements of position the
weight they deem appropriate. If any party later offers any of these materials as evidence,
Applicants may object at that time, and the ALJs may rule based on the specific material and the
purpose for which it is offered. Until then, Applicants’ objection to the ferry article, property-
search materials, hearing transcripts, and endangered-species information included only in
statements of position is premature and should be denied.
C.     Applicants do not identify any neighboring landowner testimony, and the referenced
       landowners are now represented through U3 Landowners.
       Applicants also refer generally to “other direct testimonies from his neighbors,” while
asserting that many of those materials were already filed on the Interchange. Applicants do not
identify any witness, testimony filing, Interchange item number, attached exhibit, page, line, or
particular statement supposedly objectionable. The ALJs cannot strike unspecified testimony
based on an objection to an undefined category of materials.
       Moreover, to the extent Applicants refer to filings from affected landowners aligned in
opposition to Link U3, those landowners have now joined U3 Landowners and designated 3 Trees
Ranch Family, LP as their authorized representative. The referenced materials therefore identify
the affected interests, tracts, routing positions, and impacts of the very landowners on whose behalf
Mr. Rowntree and 3 Trees Ranch now participate.
       Any duplication resulting from previously filed individual materials and the subsequent
alignment of those landowners under U3 Landowners is, at most, an administrative or cumulative-
presentation issue. It does not transform the affected landowners’ positions into inadmissible
hearsay, and it does not provide a basis to strike Mr. Rowntree’s testimony or the filings of
landowners who are now part of the aligned group. Applicants suffer no prejudice from the record
accurately reflecting the opposition and affected interests of the landowners represented through
U3 Landowners.




U3 LANDOWNERS’ RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS’ OBJECTIONS
                                                                                                   7
TO THE DIRECT TESTIMONY OF CHRIS ROWNTREE
                                         VI. PRAYER

       For the above stated reasons, U3 Landowners respectfully pray that the ALJs overrule each
of Applicants’ objections to the Direct Testimony of Chris Rowntree, deny Applicant’s motions
to strike, and grant U3 Landowners all such other and further relief as they may be justly entitled.

objection and for the ALJs to determine what evidence, if any, is being offered for an inadmissible
purpose. Applicants' category-level obj ections leave U3 Landowners and the ALJs to guess what
Applicants want removed from the record and why. The objection should therefore be overruled
as insufficiently specified. At minimum, any ruling should be confined to the specific excerpts
Applicants should not receive relief directed at unspecified attachments or unidentified portions of

B.      Applicants cannot obtain an evidentiary ruling striking material contained only in a
        statement of position.
        Applicants obj ect to an article titled "River Ferry Once Operated On Hardy Ranch Near
Lometa," unspecified "property search data," "transcripts from a 345kv line hearing," and
unspecified "chat GPT info on endangered species." These materials, however, are included in
U3 Landowners' statements of position, not in Mr. Rowntree's prefiled evidentiary testimony.
Under 16 TAC § 22.124, a statement of position is the vehicle by which a party opting not to file
testimony states its position in the proceeding. For example, intervenor Les Paul Hardy included
the ferry article in support of his position that a historic structure stands near the proposed route.
Likewise, the referenced property-search and endangered-species materials were included as
support for the affected landowners' stated positions and concerns regarding Link U3.
        Because the statements of position and their attached background materials have not been
offered as evidence, there is no hearsay, non-expert-opinion, or relevance objection for the ALJs
